vulnerability_analysis: The FoundationToken contract has two uncontrolled low-level calls that allow draining ETH: 1) swapBack() sends all contract ETH to operationsAddress, 2) withdrawStuckETH() sends all contract ETH to msg.sender (owner). Both are protected by onlyOwner modifier. The vulnerability is that if an attacker gains ownership, they can drain all ETH from the contract.
attack_strategy: 1. Gain ownership of the contract by spoofing the current owner. 2. Send ETH to the contract to give it a balance. 3. Call withdrawStuckETH() to drain all ETH to ourselves.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the current owner. 2. Call transferOwnership() to make ourselves the owner. 3. Send ETH to the contract using deal() or direct transfer. 4. Call withdrawStuckETH() as the new owner to drain ETH. 5. Verify our ETH balance increased.
